question: Who acts as the chairperson during a joint meeting of both houses of Parliament?
solution: The correct answer is __**Lok Sabha Speaker**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Lok Sabha Speaker** presides over the joint sitting of both houses of Parliament as per **Article 118** of the Indian Constitution. • A joint sitting is convened in case of a deadlock between the **Lok Sabha** and **Rajya Sabha** on specific bills. It is a method to resolve disagreements between the two houses. • The Lok Sabha Speaker holds this position as the presiding officer of the lower house and is responsible for maintaining order during the session. • If the Lok Sabha Speaker is absent, the **Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha** presides over the meeting. If both are unavailable, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha may preside. • The joint sitting provision is applicable only for **ordinary bills** and not for **constitutional amendment bills**. It is mentioned under **Article 108** of the Constitution.
